newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Telecom seeks $1.5 bln bond program.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Telecom seeks $1.5 bln bond program.

text.p: Telecom Argentina STET-France Telecom SA said on Wednesday that its board has decided to ask shareholders to approve an ongoing global bond program to $1.5 billion from $1.0 billion.

In a letter to the Buenos Aires Stock Exchange, Telecom also said it clinched a $100 million loan from a group of banks organized by Santander Investment Bank Ltd, which it will use for capital investment and debt restructuring.

The ongoing bond program first set up in June 1993 puts a cap of $1.0 billion on debt. The increase to $1.5 billion -- or its equivalent in other currencies -- will be considered at a shareholder assembly on December 16, the company said.
Telecom, which provides telecommunications services in the northern part of Argentina, is one of the two big firms operating in the country. The other is Telefonica, which covers the southern half.
The $100 million loan will be for five years and disbursed no later than December 31.
The loan will have the following rate scale --
LIBOR plus 1.50 percent on the first year
LIBOR plus 2.00 percent on the second year
LIBOR plus 2.25 percent on the third year
LIBOR plus 2.50 percent on the fourth year
LIBOR plus 2.50 percent on the fifth year.
